item: row 428: one safety copy deleted by hand, one per click (R835 (b))
key_paths: src/backup/own_net.py src/api/backup_v2.py src/backup/import_queue.py src/backup/stream_backup.py src/static/app-backup.js src/static/index.html tests/test_safety_copy_delete_row428.py
summary: The import dialog lists the safety copies in the data folder that the app recorded when it made them (name, size, date made), each with its own Delete button; others are only counted. Identity is the name plus the (device, inode, size, modification and change times) written into the copy record at creation (never a byte of the file), checked through a descriptor held on the file at delete time; a missing record or a mismatch (a link, a replaced file, a second name) refuses with could not be identified and touches nothing. Refused while an import, restore, backup, snapshot or erase (a panic wipe included) is running, asked again under the delete's lock (an unreadable source counts as running), and for every copy made after the last import run that completed (state done), by serials kept in the record, never the clock, so a clock stepped back or a restore outside the queue never frees the most recent unfinished run's copy. A record that cannot be read is never rewritten. POST with confirm, no bulk delete; the confirm names size and date, says when it is the only copy, and warns that a plaintext copy (or one not known to be encrypted) may stay recoverable on the disk. Ordinary delete wording; the freed figure is the drive's own free space measured before and after, and is not given when it did not go up (a copy cloned from the corpus shares its blocks); its at-rest record entry goes with it. Strings x12.
